timeline.event: Julius Caesar defeats Vercingetorix at the siege of Alesia

timeline.event: Charlemagne is crowned Emperor of the Romans
The Treaty of Verdun splits Charlemagne's empire among his grandsons
Hugh Capet is crowned King of the Franks
Construction of Notre-Dame de Paris begins
Joan of Arc lifts the English siege of Orléans
The St Bartholomew's Day massacre of Huguenots begins in Paris
Henry IV grants Protestants rights in the Edict of Nantes
Louis XIV moves the royal court to Versailles
Revolutionaries storm the Bastille
Napoleon crowns himself Emperor at Notre-Dame
The Eiffel Tower is completed for the World's Fair
The Lumière brothers hold the first paid public film screening
The First World War armistice is signed in a railway carriage at Compiègne
Allied troops land on the beaches of Normandy on D-Day
Charles de Gaulle founds the Fifth Republic
Concorde makes its maiden flight from Toulouse
France wins the football World Cup on home soil
Euro notes and coins replace the French franc

places.name: Paris
places.clue: Baron Haussmann's 19th-century rebuilding gave it most of its broad boulevards and cream-stone apartment blocks.

places.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
places.clue: A medieval abbey crowns this tidal island, which for centuries pilgrims could reach on foot only at low tide.

places.name: Marseille
places.clue: Founded by Greek sailors around 600 BCE, it is France's oldest city.

places.name: Lyon
places.clue: Its hidden 'traboules', passageways cut through buildings, once let silk workers carry fabric through the city out of the rain.

places.name: Nice
places.clue: Its seafront Promenade des Anglais is named after the English aristocrats who wintered here in the 1800s.

places.name: Strasbourg
places.clue: This Alsatian seat of the European Parliament has a cathedral that was the world's tallest building for over two centuries.

places.name: Chamonix
places.clue: This Alpine town beneath Mont Blanc hosted the very first Winter Olympic Games in 1924.

places.name: Lascaux
places.clue: Teenagers stumbled on this cave in 1940, its walls covered with hundreds of animals painted some 17,000 years ago.

places.name: Carcassonne
places.clue: Its walled medieval Cité was heavily restored in the 19th century by the architect Eugène Viollet-le-Duc.

places.name: Carnac
places.clue: More than 3,000 prehistoric standing stones march across its Breton fields in long parallel rows.

places.name: Dune du Pilat
places.clue: Europe's tallest sand dune rises more than 100 metres above the pine forests and the Arcachon Bay.

places.name: Bonifacio
places.clue: This Corsican old town perches on white limestone cliffs above the narrow strait that separates Corsica from Sardinia.
